body:
Correction and widening, from an independent HTTP reproduction during validation of PR #945 (2026-10-13):

- **Who can call it.** The caller needs `USERS_EDIT` and must hold everything the target permission confers. `ADMIN` is not needed; the issue body's "USERS_EDIT and ADMIN" is wrong. A caller holding only USERS_EDIT and TASKS sent `permission_id: "1\^@2"`, got 204, and the stored row was permission 12 (TASKS).
- **Not a privilege escalation.** ADR-0014's subset check runs on the purified id. A USERS_EDIT-only caller sending `"1\^@2"` gets the same 403 as sending `12`, and nothing is stored. This is an integrity defect in an authorization write. There is no permission audit table, and the raw request string is recorded nowhere.
- **The rewrite set is wider.** On `permission_id`, each of these granted 12: `"1\u000b2"`, `"1\f2"`, `"1<x>2"`, `"1<!-- c -->2"`, `"12"`, `"1\^A2"`. On `add.amount` the first five were stored as 12, and `"2\^E"` as 2. Unknown tags and comments are removed as well as control characters and entities. `"\u000b2"` and `"\f2"` (leading VT/FF) are accepted as 2.
- **Not affected:** `PUT /users/{id}/permissions`, which reads the raw body through `RolesService::Ids()` (integers only).
- **From code, not observed:** the filter also turns JSON numbers into strings (`BaseApiController.php` ~:962).

Add every input above to the regression list.
